Q: EWS API ExchnageWebServices Update() method on Contacts A:

What do you mean by "overwrite" ? if you change a property in a contact, this property will be changed, the LastModifiedTime property and ChangeKey also, maybe other properties may change ( it depends on the property you are changing, if you change the first name, it's normal that the DisplayedName change), but the ID of the contact won't change, so you can consider that the contact is not overwritten.

Q: Using form.ShowDialog() after this.Dispose(); A:

sorry, I think you can't do that, because when you call ShowDialog method, the child form becomes dependent on its parent form. so the call of dispose will be suspended until you finish with the child form.

I think you have to call the Show method and after that you can call the dispose method.

Q: Problem with php-cs-fixer after upgrade php to version 8 A:

In 2026 (php-cs-fixer v3) you can use the option:

--allow-unsupported-php-version=yes

Additionally you can also set this in config file:

<?php
$config = new PhpCsFixer\Config();
return $config->setUnsupportedPhpVersionAllowed(true);

Finally, please note that the environment variable PHP_CS_FIXER_IGNORE_ENV has been deprecated and will be removed in v4.

Q: R strptime not working for Sep in Windows 11 for some locales A:

There are sources saying that Windows 11 24H2 update changed English (New Zealand) AbbreviatedMonthName (MMM) for September from Sep to Sept:

Microsoft recently introduced a change in Windows 11 (24H2) and Server 2025 that affects the English (New Zealand) regional settings, specifically altering the abbreviation for September from "Sep" to "Sept". This change was made to align with international localization standards (CLDR), but it has caused compatibility issues with many existing systems that rely on the traditional "Sep" format. The update impacts date formatting across various applications, including POS, databases, and scripts that use the dd-MMM-yyyy format. This change in abbreviation will cause serious issues across the majority of POS functions that rely on dates and cause extreme data loss/corruption and/or stop POS from functioning altogether. 1

Windows Server 2025 with region set to NZ now gets "Sept" for month instead of "Sep", when using month format MMM. This causes exceptions in our older software, where specific formats are expected, and when parsing formatted dates into DateTime values in SQL. 2

Why did Windows 11 24H2 update change English (New Zealand) AbbreviatedMonthName (MMM) for September from Sep to Sept?

Sep Is The Short Date Format For September. Sometimes is also a good read.

Also ?strptime says about the paramater %b

Abbreviated month name in the current locale on this platform. (Also matches full name on input: in some locales there are no abbreviations of names.) Case-insensitive on input.

I can reproduce this on Windows 11 x64 (build 26100)

Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "en_NZ");  
# [1] "en_NZ"
strptime('Sep 1 2026 12:00AM', "%b %d %Y %I:%M%p")
# [1] NA
strptime('Sept 1 2026 12:00AM', "%b %d %Y %I:%M%p")
# [1] "2026-09-01 CEST"
format(as.Date("2026-09-01"), "%b")
# [1] "Sept"

In the code of Rstrptime.h in case b the locale abbreviations are obtained here and in the function get_locale_strings here.

--> It's a good thing to keep in mind that abbreviated month names vary accross locale and platform. And even in a locale they change over time.

Windows 11 - MMM - overview

loc <- c("en_GB", "en_US", "fr_FR", "de_DE", "en_KE", "en_AU", "en_NZ")
# system("locale -a", intern = TRUE) # for more options

cbind(sapply(loc, \(x) {
   Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", x)
   format(seq(as.Date("2025-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 12), "%b") |>
     iconv(from = "latin1", to = "UTF-8")
})) |> kableExtra::kbl(format = "pipe")

Q: What are these Facebook bot-like users with tfbnw.net domains? A:

I had those user accounts with email @tfbnw.net created on my website after Facebook was reviewing the access of my website because I use their API to have the feature "Login with Facebook".

I can confirm this is the internal Facebook team / bots of that team that create accounts in order to test your system, and validate some things on their site, to ensure you use their API and accesses for the intended purpose (and not, for example, for stealing user data, etc.). Those are not scammers or malicious emails, those are the Facebook support team / bots testing your system.
